items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: I went to the Louis Russell band. I stayed with Louis Russell.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's that picture where you were playing tuba.

Then I played for the Elves Parade. I was at a convention in Chicago. And I went on to Chicago. Passed through St. Louis, told Dewey I'd be back. That's when Johnny wanted me to stay with him. With all them kids. See? I joined the Drew Jackson band and stayed with the Drew Jackson band then from September 28th until February 29th. I went to the Louis Russell band. I stayed with Louis Russell. That fills that. I stayed with Louis Russell until 1940. That's when Joe fired the whole band for the Chief of Band. He…
I was going to ask about your very first records. Were you on an old record that Fate Marable made with Sidney Dez Bean and Amos White? No.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: You see, when I was in the Louis Russell band, I used to tell Russell

ctx.x: That's the kind of thing. That's the kind of thing. Well, that was that little band I had then. That's, you were doing that too? That was all ensemble. Well, there were solos. And street, street rhythm. There was background. That's right. All the time, things were happening. That's the street rhythm. See, with our band, when someone was taking a solo, there was something happening behind them. Yeah. Today, a fellow takes a solo, he's out there and left the along alone.

A 17-piece band, a 17-piece band. One guy blowing the other guy, stood up there holding the instrument. Doesn't make sense. Doesn't make sense. Doesn't make sense to me, I'll say that. You see, when I was in the Louis Russell band, I used to tell Russell, I'd say, man, you got ten of you, man. I'd say, one guy, I'd say, let's say, man, that's antique. I'd say, all right, well, it really, really, they found out why that wasn't antique.

How did all that solo business get started? I'll be darn fine, though. I don't know. I guess the public started demanding. When musicians get stars like that, everybody gets a star. I think they had to get a name.
